name: Boson (ADONE)
notes: The INFN-LNF page: 'The first evidence of an anomalous multiple production came in 1970 from the measurements of the "boson" experiment.' (a result record was not written: no publication abstract was fetchable).

Its place on the interaction straight section was later taken by the 'proton-antiproton' experiment of a Naples group; the page does not date this and the Baryon-Antibaryon experiment is recorded separately.

physics_goals.quote: The "Boson" Experiment , run by physicists from Frascati, Naples, Pavia and Rome, employed a very compact setup, made of scintillators and wire magnetostrictive chambers, well suited to detect charged particle final states under the maximum solid angle.
physics_goals.value: Charged-particle final states of e+e- annihilation over the maximum solid angle

summary.plain: One of the four first experiments at Frascati's ADONE collider (1969), by physicists from Frascati, Naples, Pavia and Rome. In 1970 it gave the first evidence of an anomalously high rate of multiple particle production in e+e- collisions.
summary.technical: Boson at ADONE (first generation, 1969): compact scintillator and magnetostrictive wire-chamber detector for charged final states; first evidence in 1970 of anomalous multiple production (later shown to be hadrons); its straight section was later taken by a Naples proton-antiproton experiment.
